chapter: Paris, Lester Young, drugs, Mississippi and later sessions
title: The improvised score for 'Buck and the Preacher'
summary: After Carter's score was rejected, guitarists and a mouth organ player improvised the soundtrack while watching the film.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But I think I told you I did some other -- I've done so many things with Benny recently. I did a movie, as a matter of fact I saw the movie last night, and -- of Sidney Potier and Harry Belafonte, 'Buck and the Preacher.' Benny wrote the whole score for this movie and they threw it out. The Poitier and Belafonte didn't want it. They wanted -- well it was a good score but they wanted something more earthy. They had -- so they got about six or seven guitars, some harmonicas, and drums and let's see, and what do you call it,
the mouth organ, the juice harp, or whatever they call the mouth organ. And it really came off good though, and everything was just spontaneous. As we saw the movie we would play, and --
Yeah, just right on the spot. You know, it came off beautifully --

Yeah, that's right, that's right. And it came off beautifully. And I'm trying to think of the guitarist. It was Howard Roberts, Al Viola, and let's see who else. Me of course, and one other guitarist, and Donald Bailey was playing drums and mouth organ.

Yeah, he plays very good mouth organ. And they had another guy by the name of Tommy Morgan, Tom Morgan. But any way it was just nice to see it because I had never seen the movie and it was on television last night, and it occurred to me how this whole background, musical background occurred. It was just a spontaneous thing.
